To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the constitutive model should be chosen to be able to describe the observed behaviour, and the numerical procedure should be selected to allow the constitutive model to describe the observed behavior.
the soil foundation structure interaction problems are best solved using a combination of the lumped parameter approach and the discrete spring approach.

(1) the stiffness and damping coefficients of the foundation system can be determined from a simplified 1D approach, which can significantly reduce the computational efforts and (2) constitutive models of soil, which are widely used for the analysis of soil structure interaction (SSI) problems, are not suitable for non linear SFSIt problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to SFSI analysis, based on a unified approach and applicabiliy of constitutive relations, which will be useful for practising engineers.
the development of a unified approach to the study of soil foundation structure interaction and the applicability of constitutve relations for sandy soils.
the development of a unified approach for modelling SFSI and the applicability of constitutitive models of soils in the context of SFSI analysis
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deformation theory based constitutive models are the most appropriate for SFSI problems.
, while constitutive models of soil are not perfect, their application is not as difficult as it is generally thought.

, in order to be used in non linear SFI analysis, constitutive models must have a sound physical basis, and must be able to capture both the rate dependent and rate independent behaviour of the material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the deformation theory based models are more suitable for the design of shallow foundations, whereas rate dependent plastic flow models can be used for deep foundation structures, where the soil response is dominated by the viscous effects.
, in order to achieve reliable results, the constitutive model for soils should be capable of capturing both the non linear elastic and inelastic behavior of soils.

the deformation theory of soil foundation structure interaction can be applied in the analysis of shallow foundations and the elasto plastic models can be used in the analysis of deep foundation systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the discrete spring model can provide a good estimate of the stiffness of the foundation, the elasto plastic model should be used for the damping.

the constitutive models for sandy soils can be successfully used in non-linear SFSI analysis, provided that the soil is not too dense, and that the soil is allowed to undergo significant shear strains.
, for the most part, deformation theory of plasticity can be used in SFSI analysis with a good accuracy and without the need to resort to more complex models.
